Your 29M estimate counts only user messages using tiktoken, while Redwood’s published guidance describes counting with the model’s tokenizer across the full request payload. So excluding system content and tool definitions can make the two totals differ; whitespace, normalization, and tool-call serialization can also contribute. You reported no retry, so retry billing doesn’t appear to explain this request.

The console confirms the recorded count, but doesn’t expose the low-level meter trace or payload needed to independently validate every token. Given the documented counting difference, I can’t conclude from this comparison alone that the meter is wrong.

I can confirm Redwood recorded **30.5 million billed tokens** for `req_p10`, but I can’t independently verify from the available meter details that this is the exact correct count.
